newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African opposition aims to form new party.
newsitem.headline: South African opposition aims to form new party.

text.p: South Africa's opposition National Party (NP) said on Wednesday it was aiming at a political movement with other groups which could lead to a new party to counter Nelson Mandela's African National Congress.

A statement released by the NP executive after a three-day meeting said the party's chief target for 1997 was to take "specific steps aimed at establishing a new political movement that might develop into a new political party".

"It will be parties which basically are in favour of free enterprise. It will be parties which are anti-communist. Obviously springs to mind the (Zulu-based) Inkatha Freedom Party and the (liberal) Democratic Party," NP leader and former president F.W. de Klerk told state television.

The NP said it was launching the new negotiation strategy and action plan for political union, expected to be drawn up by February 10, to halt the domination of President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC).
The ANC won just under two-thirds of the vote in the country's first all-race elections in 1994, ensuring it a controlling role in power.
The NP pulled out of Nelson Mandela's coalition cabinet last year saying South Africa could now benefit from a robust opposition.
